Japan's surrender unfolded in several distinct stages. Japan first offered to surrender on August 10, 1945, with the only condition being that the emperor remain the nominal head of state, after Emperor Hirohito personally broke a 3-to-3 tie vote in the Imperial Council [d3]. President Harry S. Truman then announced Japan's unconditional surrender at 7 p.m. on August 14, 1945, to reporters at the White House [d4][d8], and Emperor Hirohito broadcast the surrender to the Japanese people on August 15, 1945 [d4][d6]. The formal, legally binding surrender was signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945, at 9:04 a.m., with the ceremony lasting just 23 minutes and concluding at 0923 [d1][d6][d9]. Representatives of nine Allied nations witnessed the signing of the Instrument of Surrender, after which General MacArthur declared the war officially over [d5][d9].
